Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

immediate adjective

nearest, closest: immediate family, the immediate area

also immediate family, next of kin, close family, the immediate area, in the immediate vicinity, next (nearest)

classical

Cic. Off. 1.44: injūriōsī sunt in proximōs
Cic. Inv. 2.144: proximus cognātiōne (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 350: nearby, in proximō

proximus, proxima, proximum

adjective

nearest, next; nearest in blood

As a noun, proximī are one’s nearest relatives, the immediate family (Lewis & Short); for one’s wife and children say suī (see family). Of place, in proximō is close by, in the immediate area; of time, proximus is the last or the next (see last).

Examples

  • quī benigniōrēs volunt esse, quam rēs patitur, prīmum in eō peccant, quod injūriōsī sunt in proximōs

    those who want to be more generous than their means allow go wrong first in this, that they wrong their nearest and dearestCic. Off. 1.44

See also near, family, relative, immediate.
